AUDIO LICENCES — Mission-Based Interactive Simulation (Assets/Audio)
==============================================================================
The project has seven audio files: five animal calls (lion, leopard, elephant,
rhinoceros, buffalo), one bump sound and one savanna ambience.
Four are CC0 1.0 (Public Domain Dedication, no attribution required): the
elephant, rhino, bump and ambience files. Three are CC BY 4.0 (attribution
required, lines given below): the lion, leopard and buffalo files.
NONE is CC-BY-NC, CC-BY-SA, CC-BY-ND, or subject to any non-commercial restriction.

The sounds have been checked by measurement and spectrogram, not by ear. The
owner should listen to all seven files before release.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Species: African lion (Panthera leo) — male roaring bout (field recording)
   Output file: Assets/Audio/SFX_Lion.ogg
   Source URL (sound page): https://freesound.org/people/eardeer/sounds/458903/
   Direct file URL (preview, mp3): https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/458/458903_2155630-hq.mp3
   Title as shown: "Lion roars 1.wav"
   Description on source: "Male lions roaring. Recorded at Ukutula Game Reserve,
   South Africa. Mics used: Rode NT1A stereo pair in ORTF position. Recorder:
   Zoom H4Npro" (tags: africa, ambience, field-recording, lion, lions, nature,
   roar, south-africa, ukutula)
   Author / uploader: eardeer
   Licence: Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0), as shown on the sound page
   Licence URL: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
   Attribution required: YES. Use this line:
   "Lion roars 1.wav" by eardeer, https://freesound.org/people/eardeer/sounds/458903/, licensed under CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
   Changes made: excerpted to 4.5 s (source 39.32 s to 43.82 s; roaring onset at
   39.47 s), converted to mono, high-passed, loudness-normalised, faded.
   Known artefact: a steady tone near 4.8 kHz runs through the whole source
   (recording noise). In the excerpt it is at low level. It was not notch-filtered.
   Note: downloaded via the sound's freely accessible preview file (full
   downloads on freesound.org require a login); the preview is the same recording, lossy mp3.
   Processing: ffmpeg -n -ss 39.32 -t 4.5 -i <458903_2155630-hq.mp3> -ac 1 -ar 22050
     -af "highpass=f=40,loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5,afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.02,afade=t=out:st=4.35:d=0.15"
     -c:a libvorbis -q:a 5 SFX_Lion.ogg

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Species: Leopard (Panthera pardus) — SUBSTITUTION: jaguar (Panthera onca) "saw" call
   Output file: Assets/Audio/SFX_Leopard.ogg
   Source URL (file page): https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jaguar_saw.flac
   Direct file URL: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b4/Jaguar_saw.flac
   Title as shown: "Jaguar saw.flac"
   Description on source: "The "saw" sound made by a jaguar. The audio was extracted
   from a CC BY licensed video recorded by About Zoos at Attica Zoological Park,
   Greece." Date 2 December 2021. Source (as stated on the file page):
   https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VJ0RCZXu0v4
   Author / uploader: About Zoos
   Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, as stated on the file
   page: "This file is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0
   International license."
   Licence URL: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
   Attribution required: YES. Use this line:
   "Jaguar saw" by About Zoos, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jaguar_saw.flac, licensed under CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
   Substitution note: no leopard sawing or growl was found under an accepted
   licence. The only leopard vocalisation found, freesound "Leopard's Cough
   Isolated.wav" (drobiumdesign, sound 346402, CC BY 3.0, Pilanesberg, South
   Africa), is a 0.45 s cough and was rejected. The game's leopard model is a
   jaguar anyway. Duration is 1.39 s, shorter than the 3 to 5 s target; the source
   has no more saw calls and nothing was padded.
   Changes made: converted to mono, high-passed, loudness-normalised, faded (the
   file is not otherwise cut; it is already one call).
   Processing: ffmpeg -n -ss 0 -t 1.39 -i <Jaguar_saw.flac> -ac 1 -ar 22050
     -af "highpass=f=40,loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5,afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.02,afade=t=out:st=1.24:d=0.15"
     -c:a libvorbis -q:a 5 SFX_Leopard.ogg

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Species: African elephant (Loxodonta africana) — trumpet. NOT CONFIRMED: see note.
   Output file: Assets/Audio/SFX_Elephant.ogg
   Source URL (file page): https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Elephant_voice_-_trumpeting.ogg
   Direct file URL: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/40/Elephant_voice_-_trumpeting.ogg
   Title as shown: "Elephant voice - trumpeting.ogg"
   Description on source: "Elephant_voice_-_trumpeting. Tamil caption: யானையின் பிளிறல்
   (elephant's trumpeting/roar)". Date 1 February 2011. Source: "Own work".
   Author / uploader: தகவலுழவன் (Info-farmer), the same uploader as the lion
   recording above (Tamil Nadu, India).
   Licence: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as stated on the file page:
   "This file is made available under the Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal
   Public Domain Dedication."
   Licence URL: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
   Attribution required: NO.
   Substitution note: the page does not name the species. The uploader's other
   recording is from Tamil Nadu, India, so this is probably an Asian elephant. No
   African elephant trumpet was found under an accepted licence. Duration 1.44 s,
   shorter than the 3 to 5 s target; nothing was padded.
   Processing: ffmpeg -n -ss 0 -t 1.44 -i <Elephant_voice_-_trumpeting.ogg> -ac 1 -ar 22050
     -af "highpass=f=40,loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5,afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.02,afade=t=out:st=1.29:d=0.15"
     -c:a libvorbis -q:a 5 SFX_Elephant.ogg

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Species: white rhinoceros (Ceratotherium simum) — huffs and grunts, fighting in a waterhole
   Output file: Assets/Audio/SFX_Rhino.ogg
   Source URL (sound page): https://freesound.org/people/geoffvt/sounds/792852/
   Direct file URL (preview, mp3): https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/792/792852_3081145-hq.mp3
   Title as shown: "white Rhino   fighting"
   Description on source: "A  very unique sound of African white rhino.  Recorded
   in the Umfolozi game reserve in Kwa Zulu Natal South Africa.  @ rhino fighting
   in a waterhole."  (tags: Africa, Bush, nature, rhino, wild, wildlife)
   Author / uploader: geoffvt
   Licence: Creative Commons 0 (CC0 1.0), as shown on the sound page
   Licence URL: http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
   Attribution required: NO.
   Substitution note: the sound is a white rhinoceros, but the game's rhino model
   is a black rhinoceros (Diceros bicornis). The call stands in for the black
   rhino. The page says "fighting", so some sounds may be contact or splash sounds
   rather than calls. The 3.5 s excerpt was chosen for its low-frequency, pulsed,
   harmonic bursts.
   Level: lowered by 2 dB after processing (see the verification line of 2026-10-14).
   Clip: source 62.45 s to 65.95 s (onset of the bursts at about 62.6 s).
   Changes made: excerpted, converted to mono, high-passed, loudness-normalised, faded.
   Note: downloaded via the sound's freely accessible preview file (full
   downloads on freesound.org require a login); the preview is the same CC0 audio.
   Processing: ffmpeg -n -ss 62.45 -t 3.5 -i <792852_3081145-hq.mp3> -ac 1 -ar 22050
     -af "highpass=f=40,loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5,afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.02,afade=t=out:st=3.35:d=0.15"
     -c:a libvorbis -q:a 5 SFX_Rhino.ogg, then a 2 dB gain reduction (-2 dB).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Species: African (Cape) buffalo (Syncerus caffer) — grunts, Tanzania (birds present in source)
   Output file: Assets/Audio/SFX_Buffalo.ogg
   Source URL (sound page): https://freesound.org/people/roubignolle/sounds/35130/
   Direct file URL (preview, mp3): https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/35/35130_328279-hq.mp3
   Title as shown: "Buffles-Grognement+amb oiseaux.aif"
   Description on source: "Some buffaloes in Tanzania with birds in background
   recorded on DAT (Tascam DAP-1) with a Sennheiser ME66 by G de Courtivron."
   Author / uploader: roubignolle (recordist G de Courtivron), 21 May 2007
   Licence: Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0), as shown on the sound page
   Licence URL: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
   Attribution required: YES. Use this line:
   "Buffles-Grognement+amb oiseaux" by roubignolle (G de Courtivron), https://freesound.org/people/roubignolle/sounds/35130/, licensed under CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
   Substitution note: none on species. This is the same recording as the earlier
   buffalo file, but a different section (from 6.85 s), with a 2.5 kHz low-pass
   that reduces the birds (it does not remove them). No African buffalo recording
   free of birds was found under an accepted licence.
   Changes made: excerpted to 3.5 s, converted to mono, low-passed at 2.5 kHz,
   high-passed, loudness-normalised, faded.
   Note: downloaded via the sound's freely accessible preview file (full
   downloads on freesound.org require a login); the preview is the same CC BY audio.
   Processing: ffmpeg -n -ss 6.85 -t 3.5 -i <35130_328279-hq.mp3> -ac 1 -ar 22050
     -af "highpass=f=40,lowpass=f=2500,loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5,afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.02,afade=t=out:st=3.35:d=0.15"
     -c:a libvorbis -q:a 5 SFX_Buffalo.ogg

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Environment: African savanna (Kenya, near Voi) — daytime birds and wind ambience
   Output file: Assets/Audio/AMB_Savanna.ogg
   Source URL (sound page): https://freesound.org/people/dkaufman/sounds/743640/
   Direct file URL: https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/743/743640_21914-hq.mp3
   Sound title: "Birds and wind at Ngutuni Lodge"
   Description on source: "The sounds of the Ngutuni Lodge gardens near Voi, Kenya.
   Recorded with Sony PCM-A10 in wide mode." (location: Kaloleni, Taita–Taveta,
   Kenya; tags: birdsong, field-recording, nature; duration 0:22.165, 48 kHz stereo WAV)
   Author / uploader: dkaufman, 26 June 2024
   Licence: CC0 1.0 Universal (Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication),
   shown on the sound page as "Creative Commons 0"
   Licence URL: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
   Attribution required: NO.
   Note: downloaded via the sound's freely accessible preview file (full
   downloads on freesound.org require a login); the preview is the same CC0 audio.
   The page tags list birds and wind only (no insect tag); content was checked
   from the page description and tags, not by ear.
   Processing: ffmpeg -n -i <preview.mp3> -t 30 -af "loudnorm=I=-23:TP=-2,
   afade=t=in:st=0:d=1.5,afade=t=out:st=20.665:d=1.5" -ac 1 -ar 22050
   -c:a libvorbis -q:a 3 Assets/Audio/AMB_Savanna.ogg
   (source is 22.165 s, so -t 30 did not bite; fade-out starts at 22.165 − 1.5.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Effect: soft body thud / bump (suitable for "player walked into a rock")
   Output file: Assets/Audio/SFX_Bump.ogg
   Source URL (sound page): https://freesound.org/people/JonasTisell/sounds/496187/
   Direct file URL: https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/496/496187_3910073-hq.mp3
   Sound title: "Light Body thud (on clothing)"
   Description on source: "A light body thud used in a project of mine. feel free to
   use for anything" (tags: body, impact, thud; duration 0:00.325, 44.1 kHz stereo MP3)
   Author / uploader: JonasTisell, 7 December 2019
   Licence: CC0 1.0 Universal (Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication),
   shown on the sound page as "Creative Commons 0"
   Licence URL: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
   Attribution required: NO.
   Note: downloaded via the sound's freely accessible preview file (full
   downloads on freesound.org require a login); the preview is the same CC0 audio.
   Processing: ffmpeg -n -i <preview.mp3> -af "silenceremove=start_periods=1:
   start_duration=0.02:start_threshold=-45dB,loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5,areverse,
   afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.03,areverse" -t 0.6 -ac 1 -ar 22050 -c:a libvorbis -q:a 4
   Assets/Audio/SFX_Bump.ogg
   (30 ms fade-out implemented as areverse + fade-in + areverse, so it lands on
   the true end of the clip whatever its length.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VERIFICATION (2026-10-13): AMB_Savanna.ogg and SFX_Bump.ogg exist and are non-zero
(116,194 bytes and 4,967 bytes). Both probed as Vorbis, mono, 22050 Hz: AMB_Savanna
22.20 s; SFX_Bump 0.25 s (under the 0.6 s limit). Both sources were confirmed CC0 on
their freesound.org sound pages on 2026-10-13. Neither file is CC-BY-NC or CC-BY-SA.
Processing notes: the ambience uses the brief's settings unchanged (the source is
shorter than 30 s, so the output is the full 22.2 s). The bump uses the brief's
settings with the silence trim stated in entry 7; loudnorm cannot reach I=-16 on a
0.25 s clip, and Vorbis encoding lifted the decoded true peak to about +1.6 dBTP
(sample peak 0.0 dBFS).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VERIFICATION (2026-10-14): all seven files exist, are non-zero, and were probed as
Vorbis, mono, 22050 Hz. Durations:
Lion 4.50 s, Leopard 1.39 s, Elephant 1.44 s, Rhino 3.50 s, Buffalo 3.50 s, Bump
0.25 s, Ambience 22.20 s. Sizes: Lion 29,191; Leopard 13,397; Elephant 12,423;
Rhino 23,254; Buffalo 26,950 bytes. Mean / peak level (dB, ffmpeg volumedetect):
Lion -16.6 / -3.6; Leopard -27.1 / -1.7; Elephant -19.6 / -3.1; Rhino -17.5 / -0.2;
Buffalo -15.7 / -0.9; Bump -19.9 / -0.0; Ambience -25.2 / -4.7.
Rhino level: lowered by 2 dB after processing. Before the change the mean was
-15.6 dB and the peak 0.0 dB; after it, the mean is -17.5 dB and the peak -0.2 dB.
No file is CC-BY-NC, CC-BY-SA or CC-BY-ND.

LEVEL NOTE (2026-10-14): SFX_Leopard.ogg was raised by 9 dB and peak-limited after processing (ffmpeg volume=9dB,alimiter=limit=0.72) because it was about 10 dB quieter than the other calls.
